name: Isolation
description: The adversary is isolating his activities as much as possible to reduce the impact of any incident, such as malware infections.

subtechniques.name: App Qubes
subtechniques.description: App qubes are isolated environments in which a certain applications runs. App cubes can also be disposable, which means that they self-destruct when its originating window closes. App qubes are part of Qubes OS.

subtechniques.name: Application isolation
subtechniques.description: Applications are isolated to restrict their permissions and to reduce the impact of incidents, such as malware infections.

subtechniques.name: Attach USB to offline disposable VM
subtechniques.description: In order to prevent malware infections affecting sensitive information or systems, USB devices are only attached to offline systems or disposable virtual machines.

subtechniques.name: Dedicated email addresses
subtechniques.description: For each account or use a dedicated email address is used to segment their use and to prevent any leaks from affecting multiple accounts or services.

subtechniques.name: Dedicated laptop
subtechniques.description: A dedicated laptop for sensitive activities might be acquired to segment these activities from regular activities.

subtechniques.name: Dedicated virtual machines
subtechniques.description: Dedicated virtual machines might be used for specific purposes, e.g. sensitive activities or for accessing a forum on the Darkweb.

subtechniques.name: Emergency pause
subtechniques.description: Emergency pause is a feature in Qubes OS, which neutralized an untrusted (networked) qube while opening for example the vault for a password.

subtechniques.name: Firefox Multi-Account Containers
subtechniques.description: Firefox Multi-account containers might be used to isolate online activity in separate tabs, combined with colors to distinguish between the environments.

subtechniques.name: Offline testing
subtechniques.description: To better understand how things work and become comfortable with them, offline testing might be conducted. In addition, if unsure if software is trustworthy running it offline prevents any information leaking.

subtechniques.name: One Whonix workstation at a time for a single activity
subtechniques.description: To segment activities and prevent cross-contamination, each activity should be conducted at at time in a segmented environment.

subtechniques.name: Open all files in disposable VM
subtechniques.description: To prevent malware spreading to secure environments.

subtechniques.name: Open PDF in browser
subtechniques.description: To prevent the execution of malware with higher privileges.

subtechniques.name: Open untrusted files offline
subtechniques.description: To prevent malware spreading to other systems and leaking information.

subtechniques.name: Sandboxed Google Play
subtechniques.description: Sandboxed Google Play can be installed in GrapheneOS to prevent it from gaining access or privileges.

subtechniques.name: Sandboxing
subtechniques.description: In computer security, a sandbox is a security mechanism for separating running programs, usually in an effort to mitigate system failures and/or software vulnerabilities from spreading. The sandbox metaphor derives from the concept of a child's sandbox—a play area where kids can build, destroy, and experiment without causing any real-world damage.

procedures.name: Hybrid Analysis
procedures.description: Hybrid Analysis is a free malware analysis service for the community that detects and analyzes unknown threats using a unique Hybrid Analysis technology. https://www.hybrid-analysis.com/

subtechniques.name: Service isolation
subtechniques.description:
Isolation prevents the impact if incidents occur, therefore all services should be isolated.
